title: What happens to the human body in 49C heat? Australians are finding out
text: I think the answer is: it's not safe to be outside at 49C for any protracted period of time. Extreme heat in parts of India and Pakistan, where temperatures have exceeded 50C, has led to hundreds of deaths. "Even short periods of time in that 50C-plus environment can lead to dehydration; the heart's working hard," Hunter says. "This sort of heat stress can provoke a heart attack, it can provoke an arrhythmia – rhythm abnormalities, it can provoke circulatory collapse." In Victoria, the 2009 Black Saturday bushfires killed 173 people. "That was catastrophically bad," Hunter says.
